  "edges": [
    {
      "fromKey": "n-opw2ln",
      "toKey": "n-1gqu80",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "If the crew used a different configuration drawing or missed an unrecorded service-routing change, they would be unaware of valve states that could cause pressure loss. The lack of evidence confirming version usage (unknown status) leaves this as a plausible hypothesis for why normal procedures failed to prevent the event.",
      "status": "proposed",
      "sourceIds": ["eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the crew had confirmed they were using the correct, up-to-date configuration drawing and received a briefing on recent changes, would this have prevented the hazard scenario?",
      "competingExplanation": "The pressure loss may be due to an upstream event unrelated to valve states known to the crew (e.g., source failure), making knowledge of drawings irrelevant.",
      "evidenceGap": "No record confirms whether U-A/U-B saw recent changes or used a different version; absence does not prove they did."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-1imw4n6",
      "toKey": "n-1gqu80",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The shift log records 'boundary preparation in progress' but fails to identify the point of interruption or valve states. This lack of detail prevents understanding whether a change occurred that was not communicated, contributing to the hazard.",
      "status": "proposed",
      "sourceIds": ["24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1"],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the shift log had identified the point of interruption and valve states, would this have enabled earlier detection or prevention?",
      "competingExplanation": "The lack of detail may simply reflect incomplete logging rather than a causal link to the event.",
      "evidenceGap": "Shift logs do not identify points of interruption; no evidence links missing log details directly to the pressure loss."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-14civod",
      "toKey": "n-1gqu80",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed at notification time, indicating the boundary had not been formally released. This may have contributed to an unverified or undocumented state of equipment that led to the hazard.",
      "status": "proposed",
      "sourceIds": ["eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the maintenance acceptance signature had been signed before notification, would this have ensured a verified and documented state of equipment?",
      "competingExplanation": "Pending signatures are common in planned work; absence alone does not prove causation without evidence of an unverified condition.",
      "evidenceGap": "No record shows what specific conditions were pending or how they affected the event."
    }
  ],
  "decision": {
    "summary": "Three proposed causal links connect procedural gaps (unknown drawing version, incomplete shift log details, unsigned maintenance acceptance) to a potential unrecorded hazard scenario. All remain hypotheses due to missing evidence on whether these conditions actually existed or directly caused the pressure loss.",
    "evidenceUsed": [
      "eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1",
      "24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1"
    ],
    "unknowns": [
      "Whether crew used correct configuration drawing or saw recent changes",
      "Point of interruption in the air supply system",
      "Specific valve states at time of event"
    ],
    "alternatives": [
      "Upstream source failure unrelated to local procedures",
      "Distribution system issue not tied to maintenance boundary state"
    ],
    "confidence": 0.45
  },"evidenceRequests":[
    "claim-2x4nrr","finding-lcx7sq","claim-hpozhz"
  ]}
